_extraction_flags.notes: Excellent O-ISAC paper! Submarine cable-based photonic ISAC for coastal monitoring. φ-OTDR sensing + WDM optical communication. IEEE Network Magazine style.

reasoning_trace.step_0_visual_inspection: Fig.1: Global submarine cable map. Fig.2: Testbed at Pearl River Estuary with φ-OTDR + optical comm rack. Fig.3: f-k spectrum of ocean waves. Fig.4: P/S wave detection (Mw 4.0 earthquake). Fig.5: Regional earthquake catalog. Fig.6: Ferry tracking.
reasoning_trace.step_1_concept_analysis: System: Photonic ISAC using submarine telecommunication fiber cables. φ-OTDR (Phi-OTDR) for distributed sensing via Rayleigh backscattering. WDM separates sensing probe from data channels. Single fiber for both communication and sensing. Applications: earthquake detection, ocean wave analysis, vessel monitoring.
reasoning_trace.step_2_benchmark_verification: Sensing: f-k spectrum shows ocean waves (10 m/s, <0.3 Hz) and seismic waves (100-1000 m/s). Earthquake detection: Mw 1.1 to Mw 6.3, P-wave 5.9 km/s, S-wave 3.47 km/s. 1226 sensing elements over 10 km (8.16 m interval). 10-month continuous operation.
reasoning_trace.step_3_strategic_critique: Contribution: First photonic ISAC on submarine telecom cables. Dual-use of fiber network for comm + sensing. Long-term monitoring without additional power. Gap: Sensing limited to vibration/acoustic. Interference fading in φ-OTDR.

bibliographic.title: Photonic Integrated Sensing and Communication System Harnessing Submarine Fiber Optic Cables for Coastal Event Monitoring
bibliographic.authors: Shaoyi Chen, Kun Zhu, Jun Han, Qi Sui, Zhaohui Li

application.scenario_description: Coastal event monitoring using submarine telecommunication fiber cables: earthquake detection, ocean wave analysis, and marine ferry monitoring.

key_contribution.key_contribution: Photonic ISAC system on submarine telecommunication cables. φ-OTDR distributed sensing + WDM optical communication over single fiber without interference.
key_contribution.gap_addressed: Previous submarine sensing required dedicated cables or OBS. This reuses existing telecom infrastructure.

identification.scenario_label: Pearl River Estuary Submarine Fiber ISAC

transmitter.notes: Narrow-linewidth laser for φ-OTDR sensing. WDM data channels + monitoring channel for sensing probe. Single-end interrogation at Sanjiao Island.

receiver.notes: Coherent detection for φ-OTDR phase demodulation. Homodyne/heterodyne detection with LO from same source.

integration.notes: WDM: data channels separated from sensing channel. Both share single submarine fiber. Sensing does not interfere with communication.

waveform.notes: Comm: Standard WDM optical communication on data channels. Sensing: Coherent pulse for φ-OTDR on monitoring channel. Different wavelengths, no interference.

channel_wireless.notes: 10-13 km submarine fiber between Sanjiao Island and Guishan Island. 10 m average water depth. 10-month continuous operation.

comm_metrics.notes: Commercial optical communication service running normally during sensing experiments. Data rate not specified.

sensing_metrics.notes: 1226 channels over 10 km (8.16 m interval). Earthquake: Mw 1.1 to Mw 6.3, up to 1000+ km away. Ocean waves: 10 m/s (gravity), 100-1000 m/s (seismic). Ferry: 26 km/h tracking. 2-15 Hz bandpass for seismic.

tradeoff.notes: WDM separation eliminates comm-sensing interference. Dedicated monitoring channel for sensing. No trade-off analysis presented.
